title: Yoko Ono loses custody battle for daughter Kyoko in Texas | 1971
content:
Yoko Ono lost a custody battle for her eight-year-old daughter Kyoko on 29 September 1971.

The hearing took place at the Domestic Relations Court of Harris County, Texas. Kyoko and her father, Ono’s ex-husband Tony Cox, were living in Texas at the time.

Ono had won a custody ruling in St Thomas in the Virgin Islands on 24 September, but Cox’s lawyers successfully persuaded the Texas court to rule that its decision should take precedence. A two-day hearing began on 27 September, which Lennon and Ono did not attend.

On the second day, Cox testified that he had been harassed by Lennon and Ono, and alleged that Lennon had behaved inappropriately by taking baths with Kyoko when she was five years old. He also testified that Ono had stabbed him with scissors during their marriage, and “held me for 45 minutes in a bathtub with a broken bottle at my neck.” He claimed that Lennon and Ono were heavy drug users, and that Kyoko may have accidentally taken some of their substances.

On this day Judge Peter S Solito ruled in Cox’s favour, granting him temporary custody of Kyoko. Ono was given visitation rights of the first and third weekend in every month while in the USA, six weeks each summer, and 10 days over the Christmas period.

Following the verdict, it was reported that lawyers for Ono and Cox had reached a private agreement, which left the case subject to relitigation should either party wish.
